Sharded retained-checkpoint selectors counted record indexes within one shard file (checkpoint:<gen>:record:<n>), so the same secret text at the same record index in two shards produced one shared fingerprint; find_retained_checkpoint_finding then failed with "one secret fingerprint resolved to multiple checkpoint records" (surfaced as "could not scan retained checkpoint redaction targets"), breaking redact --finding for those retained findings and collapsing distinct copies into one fingerprint in doctor output.

Fix (1b310694): both the diagnostic scan (scan_jsonl via scan_shard_manifest) and the retained lookup (find_checkpoint_issues_in_jsonl via checkpoint_issue_paths) now build their record selector through one shared checkpoint_record_selector helper. Sharded records carry their manifest path (checkpoint:<gen>:<shard>:record:<n>); monolithic roots keep the historical checkpoint:<gen>:record:<n> shape. The helper is the single construction point, so the fingerprint doctor prints always matches what redact resolves. Receipts persist only the live semantic origin identity and acknowledgements apply only to live scans, so no persisted selector format changes and no version bump is needed; no code parses the selector shape (verified across src, tests, and the release scripts - the only consumers are starts_with("checkpoint:") classification checks). The stale cross-shard collision clause in the redact --all-blocking deferral comment now cites this fix.

Tests: identical_text_in_two_shards_yields_distinct_resolvable_findings asserts two distinct fingerprints with shard-qualified selectors, per-finding resolution to its own issue record, and a clean two-entry batch resolution (the --all-blocking path); monolithic_retained_selectors_keep_the_record_only_shape pins the unchanged monolithic selector and resolution. Mutation control: reverting the helper to the record-only shape failed the new test at the fingerprint-collision assertion, then was restored byte-for-byte. Commit 90124189 updates retained_checkpoint_issue_fingerprint_redacts_live_description, whose sharded half asserted the old shape: it now pins the generation via the checkpoint: prefix plus :record: and additionally requires a shard path (objects/) in sharded mode while keeping the exact record-only shape for monolithic; that full integration file passes 10/10, covering bead redact --finding on a retained fingerprint end-to-end in both modes.

Checklist: pre-staging git status reviewed; only this task's three files were staged (src/service/secret_diagnostics.rs, src/service/redaction.rs, tests/redaction_publication.rs); every other dirty file predates the dispatch and was left untouched. Verified the committed state, not the working tree: git archive of HEAD 90124189 into /data/build/scratch/beadrs-4b5ee36b-verify-JykPqP, where scripts/definition-of-done.sh ran to completion (PASS: fmt + clippy + test, exit 0; zero FAILED/panicked lines in its log) and the two acceptance cargo test lines were re-run with a private target directory; the extraction and its gate target directory were removed after success. Two earlier background starts of the same script were stopped by the harness 600-second background time limit mid-suite and were restarted; the final complete run is the evidence here. git push exit=0 (1690e1de..90124189); git rev-list origin/main..HEAD exit=0 with empty output.

```verified:

cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings exit=0
cargo test exit=0
cargo test --lib service::secret_diagnostics exit=0

```

This attempt re-verified the committed state instead of re-editing: the acceptance grep for run_verify_before_close over src returns no matches in the shared worktree, at HEAD, and inside a clean git-archive extraction of HEAD (exit 1 = no matches, which is the pass condition).

Why attempts 1 and 2 bounced, and why that is gone: gate_0 is the workspace-run cargo check declared in .needle.yaml (run_in: workspace), so it compiles the shared tree including rival dispatches' uncommitted in-flight edits, and the close-time suite inherits whatever state the concurrent beadrs-4b5ee36b landing left on main. Both hazards came from that landing: an arity break in uncommitted edits (bounced attempt 1's gate at 20:58Z, landed fixed as 1b310694) and a one-test red on main (failed this attempt's first DOD, fixed by the owner as 90124189). Neither defect ever touched the deliverable; the identical workspace check was re-run by this attempt immediately before closing (exit 0).

Final verification ran against a clean git-archive extraction of committed HEAD 90124189, which contains 802e8602. cargo build --all-targets exit 0 with fresh Compiling lines; scripts/definition-of-done.sh --fast (cargo fmt --check + full cargo test) exit 0; acceptance grep exit 1 (no matches).
